name: Beanstalk
loss_note: $181M drained, about $76M kept by the attacker
tldr: Voting power was counted at the moment of the vote. The attacker borrowed a huge amount with a flash loan, voted his own proposal through, and paid the loan back.
what: Beanstalk was a stablecoin protocol governed by its token holders, with an emergency way to execute proposals quickly.
happened: The attacker flash-borrowed enough tokens for a supermajority, passed a proposal that sent the treasury to himself, executed it, and repaid the loan, all in one transaction.
bug: Votes were measured "right now", and a passed proposal could execute immediately, with no delay.
prevent: Measure voting power at an earlier snapshot and add a timelock between approval and execution.
lesson: Anything measured in the current block can be borrowed for one block.

sources.title: Atlantis Loans - REKT (on Beanstalk's missing delay)
